components.description: Paid time off after childbirth for the faculty member who gives birth: eight weeks after delivery (longer if a physician certifies), paid at base salary through the University sick leave and short-term disability policies (Handbook II.E.4; HR Policy 613.3).
components.mechanism_note: V1 three-part test met: a childbirth-specific period (after delivery), a length (8 weeks) and a pay level (sick pay and STD are continuation of base salary). Paid through the sick-leave reserve (renewed each July 1, an employer plan under R1) and STD.
components.faculty_group_note: Handbook: "A faculty member who gives birth"; Policy 613: "Full-time faculty ... are eligible for sick leave and short-term disability benefits"
components.eligible_parent_wording: A faculty member who gives birth; Medical leave resulting from pregnancy
components.entitlement_note: Policy 613: "shall entitle employees ... to paid leave for eight (8) weeks after delivery"; the handbook's "normally is entitled" qualifies the length (8 weeks, or longer if certified), not the grant.
components.duration_note: Eight weeks after delivery, or longer as medically necessary when certified by the physician (R10: coded as a minimum). The longer period is bounded by Policy 613's one month of sick leave plus five months of combined PTO and STD in 12 months (Policy 631: STD up to six months / 132 work days); no childbirth-specific maximum is stated, so no duration_max is coded.
components.medical_certification_note: A period longer than eight weeks requires physician certification; STD days are paid for a continuous, incapacitating condition certified by a physician.
components.pay_fraction: continuation of base salary and benefits
components.relief_note: Recipients of Policy 613 benefits are prohibited from working anywhere.

mechanism: Medical leave resulting from pregnancy shall entitle employees under this policy to paid leave for eight (8) weeks after delivery, or the length of time determined to be medically necessary as certified by the employee's physician.

components.description: A Standing Faculty member who is the primary caregiver of a newly arrived child (birth or adoption) is entitled, without reduction in pay, to a 50% reduction in teaching in one academic year (often a semester without teaching), starting within six months of the birth or arrival; research, committee work and advising continue.

components.description: Unpaid, job-protected leave of up to 12 weeks in a 12-month period under the federal FMLA (HR Policy 631) for the birth and care of a child, adoption or foster placement, the employee's own serious health condition (including pregnancy), or care of a spouse, child or parent with a serious health condition.
components.faculty_group_note: Policy 631 Applicability: All Faculty & Staff; "Employee means faculty or staff member"
components.eligible_parent_wording: The birth and care of the employee's child; Placement with the employee of a child for adoption or foster care; FMLA applies equally to male and female employees
components.duration_note: Up to 12 weeks in a 12-month period measured backward; the statute grants 12 workweeks (29 U.S.C. 2612(a)(1)). The 26-workweek military caregiver leave is not a parental provision (listed under C4 not_components).
components.service_requirement: 12 months of employment and 1,250 hours in the preceding 12 months; worksite with 50 or more employees within 75 miles

notes: Birth parent chain: childbirth paid time off 8 weeks (c1; FMLA c3 alongside from its start, up to 12 weeks) -> Faculty Parental Policy teaching relief, one semester commencing within six months of the birth (c2). Sick leave c5 -> STD c6 -> unpaid leave Policy 616 c9 is the generic medical path; c1 is paid through it.

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 weeks (c3) with up to 5 paid sick days (c4) and PTO substitution (c8) within it; Faculty Parental Policy teaching relief (c2) if primary caregiver, placed by the default order (no stated link to FMLA).

Documents named but not saved: HR Policies 404 (STD), 405 (LTD), 412 (New Child Policy), 603 (Attendance), 607 (Paid Time Off), 612 (Sick Leave), 614, 616 (Leave of Absence Without Pay), 629 (Termination), 714, 001, 112; FMLA Guide for Faculty and Staff and FMLA FAQ; Division of Human Resources Policy Manual; domestic partner benefits policy; the "child care leave" named in Handbook II.E.4; Postdoctoral Trainee Policy (Almanac link). Policy 412 (New Child Policy) may hold further parental provisions.

Reference date 2018-04-12: Handbook 2017 version (revised July 1, 2017), Policy 613 effective 10/24/2016 and Policy 631 effective 07/01/2016 (successor effective 06/16/2018) are in force on that date per their version notes.

Not components: scholarly leaves (require a programme of study or research) and leaves for employment elsewhere (II.E.2); phased retirement; catastrophic-event tenure extension (II.E.3, not parent-related).

paid_caps.note: combined cap 5 months on PTO and STD (c8, c6) in a 12-month period
